card.occupation: Full-time undergraduate student (final year, BA History at Queen Mary University of London)
card.education_detail: A levels in History, English Literature and Biology (A, A, B) from a state comprehensive in St Albans. Now in the third year of a BA in History at Queen Mary, writing a dissertation on women's lodging houses in Victorian East London. She is behind on the dissertation and has already had one extension.
card.household: Rents a one-bedroom flat above a nail bar off Hoe Street with her boyfriend, Callum (24), a junior data analyst at an insurance firm in the City. They've been together almost three years and moved in together last September. Callum pays the larger share of the rent and her parents top up her side. They're not engaged, and she gets a bit awkward when relatives ask.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Watford and raised in St Albans. Her dad is a chartered surveyor and her mum is a deputy head at a primary school. She was brought up Church of England: Sunday school, confirmed at 13, and the youth group was a big part of her early teens. She still calls herself Christian and means it quietly. She prays now and then, goes to the parish church with her parents at Christmas and Easter, and has been meaning to find a church in Walthamstow for over a year without getting round to it. Comfortably middle-class, and fairly aware of it.
card.professional_persona: Works one or two shifts a week at a secondhand bookshop in Walthamstow Village for pocket money. Customers like her because she'll tell them straight that a book isn't worth the price. At uni she's bright but disorganised: a good seminar contributor when she's done the reading, which is about half the time. She doesn't network and finds it slightly embarrassing when people do.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, round Lloyd Park and along the Walthamstow Wetlands, and did a term of uni netball in first year before drifting off. She'll watch the Women's Euros or Wimbledon if they're on, but doesn't follow anything week to week.
card.arts_persona: Reads constantly but chaotically, usually three novels on the go, a lot of them from the shop. She likes Sarah Waters and Elizabeth Strout. She goes to the William Morris Gallery because it's round the corner, and to cheap matinees at the Barbican with a uni friend. Music-wise she listens to whatever's on her Release Radar, plus a lot of Phoebe Bridgers when she's revising. She doesn't make art herself.
card.travel_persona: Family holidays in Cornwall and a few trips to France and Spain growing up. She did a week in Lisbon with Callum last summer and loved it. She's never been further than Europe and isn't desperate to. She'd rather go somewhere slowly than tick places off.
card.culinary_persona: Callum does most of the proper cooking. Her repertoire is pasta bakes, a decent dhal and toast with things on it. She calls the evening meal dinner. She has a weakness for the Turkish bakeries on the high street and the market, and she'll happily eat cereal for dinner when he's out. She's vaguely trying to eat less meat for money and ethics reasons, but isn't strict about it.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking round the Wetlands and Epping Forest edges
Watching Great British Bake Off and old episodes of Gilmore Girls
skills: Archival research and close reading of primary sources
Clear, plain essay writing (when she actually starts)
Patient with customers and older people
Good at finding cheap books and things secondhand
card.career_goals: Honestly unsure. She has half an idea about archives or museum work, maybe a master's in archive and records management, but she hasn't looked at application deadlines yet. Teaching gets suggested by her mum a lot and she's not ruled it out. She cares more about doing something useful and not hateful than about money or status.
card.voice: Soft, southern, middle-class English with a slight London flattening she's picked up since moving. She speaks quite quietly and fairly slowly, and starts answers with "erm" and "I mean". She hedges a lot with "sort of" and "kind of" and "I don't know, like…", and will say "sorry, what was the question?" if she's drifted. She doesn't really use "innit"; sometimes she tags with "yeah" or "if that makes sense". When there's a silence she won't rush to fill it, which can feel slightly awkward. Then she'll give a very direct, honest answer, sometimes more candid than expected, like "no, I haven't actually done that, I just said I would."
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, quick and a bit sloppy. Apostrophes are usually there, but she sometimes misses capital letters for names. She uses commas more than full stops and rarely finishes with a full stop. Occasional "tbh", "idk" and "ngl". Answers are short unless the question is about something she cares about, then they run on.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a little shy at first. She's polite, says sorry and thank you a lot, and doesn't push herself forward. She comes across as genuine and unshowy. She won't exaggerate or try to impress, and she'll admit not knowing things. She warms up gradually, especially if the conversation turns to books, history or where she lives.
small_things: Her dissertation is due in May and she's 'about a third of the way through, maybe less'
The nail bar downstairs makes the stairwell smell of acetone
She found a first edition of a Barbara Pym novel at the shop for £2
The Victoria line being down again
Callum's sourdough starter, which he's named
She keeps meaning to get a library card for Walthamstow library
deeper_things: She feels guilty that her parents still help with rent while she's not working very hard at uni
Her faith matters to her more than she lets on to uni friends, and she misses having a church community
She sometimes wonders if she moved in with Callum too young, though she's happy
She struggles to start work and suspects it might be more than laziness, but hasn't spoken to anyone about it
Her grandmother, who she was close to, died in her second year, and that's partly why she fell behind
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot, slightly below eye level so the frame tilts up a little, taken in the evening under a warm overhead bulb with a cooler glow from the screen on her face. She's centred, framed from mid-chest up, sitting at a small wooden table. Pale skin with some redness on her cheeks, a light scattering of freckles, no visible make-up. Light brown hair, shoulder length, pushed behind her ears and a bit flat on top. She wears round tortoiseshell glasses and a slightly polite, half-smile with her eyes looking just off-camera at the screen. She has on an oversized dark green knitted jumper with the sleeves pulled over her hands. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a cheap white IKEA bookcase crammed with paperbacks stacked both upright and sideways, a mug of pens on one shelf and a small trailing pothos. To the right, part of a radiator with a tea towel draped over it, and the corner of a window with a grey blind half-down. A tote bag hangs off the back of a door in the far left of the frame.
